📝 Sometimes They Return 📝 It suddenly turned out that yet another ex-Azov member, who sat in captivity after Mariupol , received a relatively high position in the AFU. Bohdan "Taur" Krotevych, former chief of staff of the Azov brigade, took command of the 42nd Separate Marine Infantry Brigade of the AFU. It would be strange to ask where the Ukrainian army got so many "Azov members," and even in the ranks of command. Many returned to the ranks of Kyiv regime formations after exchanges and have been fighting since 2022. The only thing that changed was the format with the transition from brigades to corps. Media promotion is easily explained. The corps shows the best results among the AFU on the battlefield and is better supplied than other units — it has ground robotic systems and drones in abundance. And against the backdrop of personnel reductions and losses of ideological cadres over the years of the SMO, the "Azov members" remained a resource and a showcase demonstrating that Ukrainian formations continue to function. ❗️ The appointment specifically to the 42nd Marine Infantry Brigade is a much more interesting story. This unit was not particularly noted anywhere before, and the direction where it will be sent allows for speculation about the enemy's plans. Formally, they are part of the 30th Marine Infantry Corps, oriented toward the Dnipro direction, but in fact they have been thrown at various sectors. And the appearance of a potential assault marine unit with "Azov" approaches could be a very interesting marker. 📌 Krotevych himself, by the way, was once favored by Russian media. In August of '25, his interview with criticism of Syrsky and mobilization was widely circulated in headlines, and as recently as July '26 he spoke about the defeat of so-called Ukraine and thousands of losses in the assault battalions created by Syrsky. So what has changed now? A question, as they say, with an asterisk. #Ukraine ✉ MAX 💸 Support us Original msg

🇺🇸 🇲🇽 Mexico accuses US of meddling and allowing drugs to flood American streets Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has accused US law enforcement agencies of meddling in Mexico’s internal affairs under the war on drugs pretext while allowing more than a million illicit fentanyl pills to enter the US. Earlier, the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) announced the launch of anonymous tip lines in Mexico to crack down on drug cartels. 👉 However, DEA whistleblowers revealed in June that the agency knowingly let 1.4 million counterfeit fentanyl pills go unseized between August 2024 and April 2025 to track a drug trafficking ring operating across the US southwest. Sheinbaum denounced the initiative as “Fast and Furious for Fentanyl,” referring to an Obama-era operation that ended in a political scandal. From late 2009 to early 2011, US law enforcement agencies allowed roughly 2,000 firearms to be smuggled into Mexico in the hope of tracing high-ranking cartel leaders. Hundreds of the weapons were later recovered in the US, including two linked to the 2010 murder of Border Patrol Agent Brian Terry. Western Hemisphere control? The US has repeatedly sought to interfere in Mexico’s counter-narcotics operations, according to CBS News. At one point, the Trump administration proposed deploying US troops to Mexico, arguing that the country was incapable of reining in drug lords. Sheinbaum rejected the offer while remaining open to cooperation with Washington, “but without subordination.” 👉 On November 20, Mexico captured drug lord Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, who is on the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list, but firmly rejected extraditing him to the US. Mexico also refused to arrest Sinaloa Governor Ruben Rocha Moya at Washington’s request after US federal prosecutors unsealed a drug trafficking indictment against him. ❗️ Critics argue that the US is undermining the sovereignty of Latin American states by prosecuting foreign nationals on drug charges, abducting them, launching military operations under the pretext of combating drug trafficking, as in Venezuela, and backing regional allies’ military interventions in neighboring countries, as El Salvador did in Haiti . 👍 Substack | Chat | @geopolitics_prime
